https://mbcaustin.org/event-6867084.description: Mando Rayo, Taco Journalist Tacos of Texas Podcast United Tacos of America About the Program: Tacos of Texas: A Journey Through Foodways, People and Traditions About the Speaker: Mando Rayo’s experience is deep-rooted in Latinx & BIPOC communities and is a James Beard Foundation Awards finalist and winner of two Signal Awards for podcasting. Mando is a digital story-teller and uses his Latinx identity to inspire and build bridges through his production company, IDENTITY. From working with PBS ITVS, El Rey Network, 7-Eleven/Laredo Taco Company, Beef Loving Texans, Whataburger, People en Español y más, Mando shares stories through food, culture, documentaries and digital platforms. As a Taco Journalist, food explorer and street ethnographer, Mando has traveled across the U.S. to uncover the tastiest tacos, from the Rio Grande Valley in Texas to L.A. and New Orleans to New York City. Mando is the producer and co-author of the books, 'Austin Breakfast Tacos' and ‘The Tacos of Texas' (University of Texas Press) & docu-series with PBS Digital Studios, United Tacos of America TV Show on El Rey Network and the Vitamina T for Tacos children’s book series (Jade Publishing). Mando ’s work has been featured on Bon Appetit Magazine, The Food Network, NPR, The New York Times and SXSW. You can listen to El Seis - Season 6 of the Tacos of Texas Podcast on KUT, Austin's NPR Station and Texas Standard, or wherever you get your podcasts. https://mbcaustin.org/event-6871786.description: Jeremi Suri image https://lbj.utexas.edu/sites/default/files/profilephotos/JeremiSuri_2022.jpg Jeremi Suri, UT Global Affairs Professor About the Program: Mid-term Elections: A Historical Perspective and View Forward About the Speaker: Jeremi Suri holds the Mack Brown Distinguished Chair for Leadership in Global Affairs at The University of Texas at Austin. He is a professor in the University's Department of History and the LBJ School of Public Affairs. Dr. Suri is the author and editor of eleven books on contemporary politics and foreign policy, most recently link https://www.publicaffairsbooks.com/titles/jeremi-suri/civil-war-by-other-means/9781541758544/ Civil War By Other Means: America's Long and Unfinished Fight for Democracy. His other books include link https://www.basicbooks.com/titles/jeremi-suri/the-impossible-presidency/9780465051731/ The Impossible Presidency: The Rise and Fall of America's Highest Office; link https://www.hup.harvard.edu/catalog.php?isbn=9780674032521 Henry Kissinger and the American Century; link https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/Libertys-Surest-Guardian/Jeremi-Suri/9781439119136 Liberty's Surest Guardian: American Nation-Building from the Founders to Obama; and link https://global.oup.com/academic/product/foreign-policy-breakthroughs-9780190226121?cc=us&lang=en& Foreign Policy Breakthroughs: Cases in Successful Diplomacy (with Robert Hutchings). Dr. Suri writes for major newspapers and magazines including the New York Times, Washington Post, Los Angeles Times, New York Daily News, Dallas Morning News, Houston Chronicle, Boston Globe, The Atlantic, Foreign Policy, Foreign Affairs, Fortune, The American Prospect and Wired — as well as for various online sites and blogs. He is a popular public lecturer, and appears frequently on radio and television. Dr. Suri teaches courses on strategy and decision-making, leadership, globalization, international relations and modern history. He teaches graduate and undergraduate courses, and he teaches and serves as academic director for the link https://empl.lbj.utexas.edu/ Executive Master in Public Leadership program (EMPL) at LBJ. His research and teaching have received numerous prizes. In 2007 Smithsonian magazine named him one of America's "Top Young Innovators" in the arts and sciences. In 2018 he received the Pro Bene Meritis Award for Contributions to the Liberal Arts. In the same year also received the President’s Associates Teaching Excellence Award from the University of Texas at Austin. https://mbcaustin.org/event-6871902.description: Bridget Grumet, Editorial Page Editor, Austin American-Statesman About the Program: What's the latest in Austin and in Texas? Come hear award-winning journalist, three-time recipient of the Carmage Walls Commentary Prize (most recently this year!), and Statesman Editorial Page Editor Bridget Grumet to find out! About the Speaker: Bridget Grumet is the Editorial Page Editor for the Austin American-Statesman, where she has served as an editorial board member since 2018. She has received numerous national awards, including the National Headliner Award for local newspaper columns and the Sigma Delta Chi Award for general column writing, and she's a three-time winner of the Carmage Walls Commentary Prize. Her work covers a wide range of issues, including police use of force, efforts to address homelessness, access to health care and ensuring voters can participate in their democracy. In her previous role as Metro columnist, and now running the editorial page, she seeks to highlight untold stories and hold leaders accountable. https://mbcaustin.org/event-6897971.description: Leana Mann, Chief Appraiser, Travis Central Appraisal District About the Program: Property taxes are the largest source of tax revenue in Texas, and the process all starts with the appraisal. Leana Mann will give us a window into how it all works with her insights and stories about this most fundamental tax bill all property owners face. About the Speaker: Leana Mann currently serves as the Chief Appraiser of the Travis Central Appraisal District. A graduate of Texas State University, Mann has more than a decade of experience with TCAD and has held a variety of positions with the District, including staff accountant, Finance and Facilities Director, Deputy Chief of Operations, and Deputy Chief Appraiser. She is a Certified Government Finance Officer (CGFO), Certified Chief Appraiser (CCA), and Registered Professional Appraiser (RPA). She has served as Chief Appraiser since March 2024.
